data.name: NewProject
data.comment: A command bar button (with an icon) that starts a new, empty project; also its screen reader name. Keep it to about 16 characters: the command bar is full at the smallest window (640 px).

data.name: UnsavedChangesName
data.comment: The screen reader name of the dot in the title bar that shows while the project has unsaved changes.

data.name: InspectorTabsName
data.comment: The screen reader name of the row of tabs (Timing, Frame, Output) in a narrow window: which settings panel shows.

data.name: StartRegionName
data.comment: The screen reader name of the first-launch screen's main region (a landmark): the start screen.

data.name: StageRegionName
data.comment: The screen reader name of the editing screen's main region (a landmark): the preview, its play controls and the filmstrip. A noun.

data.name: InspectorRegionName
data.comment: The screen reader name of the region (a landmark) that holds the Timing, Frame and Output panels.

data.name: RegionLandmarkType
data.comment: What a screen reader calls a region that is no standard landmark (the filmstrip, the export panel): the ARIA word "region" in your language, lower case as Narrator reads it.

data.name: SentenceJoin
data.comment: Two texts read one after the other, for a screen reader announcement or a notice: {0} the first sentence, {1} the next ("Rounded to 37.48 fps." and "742 photos → 24.7 s at 30 fps"). Also joins the two lines of the Timing readout into one ({0} "742 photos → 24.7 s", {1} "at 30 fps"). A space in most languages.

data.name: WindowTitleSaved
data.comment: The window title of a project with nothing unsaved. {0} the project name ("Harbor sunset"), {1} the product name (10Lapse).

data.name: WindowTitleUnsaved
data.comment: The window title while there are unsaved changes; the dot marks them. {0} the project name, {1} the product name (10Lapse).

data.name: NewProjectTitle
data.comment: The title of the dialog New project opens when there is work to lose.

data.name: NewProjectMessageNoPhotos
data.value: This project's settings will be cleared.
data.comment: The New project dialog's message for a project with changed settings but no photos.

data.name: NewProjectMessage_one
data.value: This project's photo and settings will be cleared. The photo file stays on your PC.
data.comment: The New project dialog's message for a project with photos. {0} the number of photos: English leaves {0} out because the count is always 1 here (a project without photos has its own message); leave it out too.

data.name: NewProjectMessage_other
data.value: This project's {0} photos and settings will be cleared. The photo files stay on your PC.
data.comment: The New project dialog's message for a project with photos. {0} the number of photos ("742").

data.name: NewProjectConfirm
data.comment: A dialog button that clears the project and starts a new one (in the New project dialog and the drop dialog). Keep it to about 20 characters: the drop dialog's three buttons share its width.

data.name: Cancel
data.comment: A dialog button that closes the dialog and keeps everything as it is; also the button that stops an import. Keep it short (about 12 characters).

data.name: InfoBarActionFailed
data.value: That couldn't be done because of an unexpected problem. Try again, and restart 10Lapse if it keeps happening.
data.comment: A message bar shown when a message bar's own button failed.

data.name: InfoBarShowDetails
data.comment: A message bar's button that shows the list under it (the photos it is about). Keep it to about 14 characters.

data.name: InfoBarHideDetails
data.comment: The same button while the list shows. Keep it to about 14 characters.

data.name: InfoBarDismiss
data.comment: The screen reader name of a message bar's close (×) button.

data.name: ErrorUnexpected
data.value: Something unexpected stopped that. Try again, and if it keeps happening, copy the diagnostics into a bug report.
data.comment: A message bar for a failure with no cause the user can act on. It offers the Copy diagnostics button.

data.name: ErrorUnhandled
data.value: 10Lapse ran into an unexpected problem and kept running. If something looks wrong, restart 10Lapse.
data.comment: A message bar for a failure nothing caught, after which the app kept running.

data.name: ErrorFileNotFoundNamed
data.value: {0} couldn't be found. It may have been moved, renamed or deleted; check that it's still there, then try again.
data.comment: A message bar: a file is gone. {0} the file name ("IMG_4402.JPG").

data.name: ErrorFileNotFound
data.value: A file couldn't be found. It may have been moved, renamed or deleted; check that it's still there, then try again.
data.comment: A message bar: a file is gone and its name is not known.

data.name: ErrorFolderNotFound
data.value: A folder couldn't be found. Check that it still exists and that its drive is connected, then try again.
data.comment: A message bar: a folder, drive or network share is gone.

data.name: ErrorPathTooLong
data.value: A file's path is too long for Windows. Move it to a folder with a shorter path, then try again.
data.comment: A message bar: a path longer than Windows allows.

data.name: ErrorAccessDenied
data.value: Windows didn't let 10Lapse open a file or folder. Check that you have access to it, or choose another place, then try again.
data.comment: A message bar: access denied, or the place is write-protected.

data.name: ErrorFileInUse
data.value: A file is open in another app. Close it there, then try again.
data.comment: A message bar: another app holds a file 10Lapse needs.

data.name: ErrorDiskFull
data.value: The disk is full. Free up some space or choose another drive, then try again.
data.comment: A message bar: the disk is full.

data.name: ErrorOutOfMemory
data.value: Your PC ran out of memory. Close some other apps, then try again.
data.comment: A message bar: out of memory.

data.name: ErrorDriveDisconnected
data.value: The drive or network folder was disconnected. Connect it again, then try again.
data.comment: A message bar: a removable drive or network share went away while in use.

data.name: ErrorCannotRead
data.value: A file can't be read: its drive or memory card may be damaged. Copy the photos to another drive, then try again.
data.comment: A message bar: a file's data cannot be read (a damaged disk or card).

data.name: ErrorClipboardBusy
data.value: Another app is using the clipboard. Try again in a moment.
data.comment: A message bar: another app holds the clipboard open.

data.name: ExportFailedEncoderUnavailable
data.value: Windows couldn't load a video encoder. Install the latest Windows updates and graphics driver, then export again.
data.comment: A message bar after a failed export: no H.264 encoder loads.

data.name: ExportFailedSettingsRejected
data.value: The video encoder doesn't accept these settings. Choose a lower resolution or frame rate, then export again.
data.comment: A message bar after a failed export: the encoder refused the size, frame rate or bitrate.

data.name: ExportFailedEncoder
data.value: The video encoder stopped with an error. Export again, and update your graphics driver if it keeps happening.
data.comment: A message bar after a failed export: the encoder failed for another reason.

data.name: ExportFailedEncoderStalled
data.value: The video encoder stopped responding. Export again, and update your graphics driver if it keeps happening.
data.comment: A message bar after a failed export: the encoder stopped taking frames.

data.name: ExportFailedEncoderStuck
data.value: An earlier export left the video encoder stuck. Restart 10Lapse, then export again.
data.comment: A message bar: the encoder could not open while an earlier export's encoder is still stuck.

data.name: ExportFailedFolderNotWritable
data.value: 10Lapse can't save videos in that folder. Choose another folder, then export again.
data.comment: A message bar after a failed export: the chosen folder cannot be written to.

data.name: ExportFailedFileInUse
data.value: The video file is open in another app. Close it there, then export again.
data.comment: A message bar after a failed export: another app has the video file open.

data.name: ExportFailedFolderMissing
data.value: The folder for the video can't be found. Connect its drive or choose another folder, then export again.
data.comment: A message bar after a failed export: the chosen folder, drive or share is not there.

data.name: ExportFailedDiskFull
data.value: The disk is full. Free up some space or choose a folder on another drive, then export again.
data.comment: A message bar after a failed export: the disk is full.

data.name: ExportFailedNoGraphicsDevice
data.value: This PC has no graphics device that can export video. Update your graphics driver, then export again.
data.comment: A message bar after a failed export: no graphics device can run it.

data.name: ExportFailedGraphicsDeviceLost
data.value: The graphics driver reset during the export. Export again, and update your graphics driver if it keeps happening.
data.comment: A message bar after a failed export: the driver reset or the graphics card went away.

data.name: ExportFailedOutOfMemory
data.value: There isn't enough memory to export. Close some other apps or choose a lower resolution, then export again.
data.comment: A message bar after a failed export: not enough system or video memory.

data.name: ExportFailedPhotoUnreadable
data.value: A photo in the project can't be read. Remove it or fix the file, then export again.
data.comment: A message bar after a failed export: a photo could not be loaded, and the app does not know which.

data.name: ExportFailedPhotoUnreadableNamed
data.value: Photo {0}, {1}, can't be read ({2}). Remove it from the project or fix the file, then export again.
data.comment: A message bar after a failed export. {0} the photo's place in the video, from 1 ("312"), {1} its file name ("IMG_4402.JPG"), {2} why, as a short reason from SkippedFileText ("Damaged file").

data.name: ExportFailedPhotoUnreadableNamedNoReason
data.value: Photo {0}, {1}, can't be read. Remove it from the project or fix the file, then export again.
data.comment: A message bar after a failed export. {0} the photo's place in the video, from 1 ("312"), {1} its file name.

data.name: ExportFailedDrawing
data.value: 10Lapse couldn't draw a frame of the video. Export again, and update your graphics driver if it keeps happening.
data.comment: A message bar after a failed export: drawing a frame (one picture of the video) failed on the graphics device.

data.name: ExportSavedBesideFormat
data.value: {0} is open in another app, so the video was saved as {1}.
data.comment: A message bar after an export: the chosen file was held by another app. {0} the file name asked for ("Harbor.mp4"), {1} the file name written ("Harbor (2).mp4").

data.name: CopyDiagnostics
data.comment: A button (in a message bar and on the Settings page) that copies technical details for a bug report to the clipboard. Keep it to about 20 characters.

data.name: DiagnosticsCopied
data.value: Diagnostics copied. Paste them into a GitHub issue or an email.
data.comment: A message bar after Copy diagnostics worked.

data.name: StartupFailed
data.value:
10Lapse couldn't start because of an unexpected problem. Restart your PC and try again; if it keeps happening, reinstall 10Lapse from the Microsoft Store.
The log is in {0}.
data.comment: A Windows message box when the window cannot be created at start-up. {0} the log folder's full path. Keep the blank line.

data.name: SettingsTitle
data.comment: The heading of the Settings page (the app's preferences).

data.name: SettingsButton
data.comment: The screen reader name and tooltip of the command bar's gear button that opens the Settings page. Usually the same word as SettingsTitle.

data.name: Back
data.comment: The command bar button that leaves the Settings page and goes back to the project.

data.name: SettingsAboutSection
data.comment: A section heading on the Settings page, over the Feedback and Diagnostics cards: about the app.

data.name: DiagnosticsCardTitle
data.comment: The title of the Settings card that copies technical details for a bug report.

data.name: DiagnosticsCardCaption
data.value: Copies the app and Windows versions, your graphics card, the video encoders and the last 200 log lines, to paste into a bug report. The log lines can name files and folders 10Lapse worked with, never the photos themselves. Nothing is sent from your PC.
data.comment: The text under the Diagnostics card's title. It describes the Copy diagnostics button next to it.

data.name: SettingsDefaultsSection
data.comment: A section heading on the Settings page, over the card that resets the remembered settings.

data.name: ResetCardTitle
data.comment: The title of the Settings card that resets the remembered settings.

data.name: ResetCardCaption
data.value: 10Lapse starts each project with your last speed, frame shape and output. This puts them back to what a fresh install has, in the project you have open too, and forgets the folders it opens in. Your photos are not touched.
data.comment: The text under the reset card's title.

data.name: ResetButton
data.comment: The reset card's button (a verb). Keep it to about 12 characters.

data.name: ResetDone
data.value: Settings are back to their defaults.
data.comment: A message bar after the reset.

data.name: TimingHeadline_one
data.comment: The first, larger line of the Timing panel's readout: the photos make a video this long. {0} the number of photos ("1"; in French and Brazilian Portuguese also "0"), {1} the video's length ("0.5 s"). It must read on its own; TimingDetail follows on the next line (or after SentenceJoin for a screen reader). Keep it to about 24 characters with numbers: the panel is 280 px wide.

data.name: TimingHeadline_other
data.comment: The first, larger line of the Timing panel's readout. {0} the number of photos ("742"), {1} the video's length ("24.7 s", "2 min 47 s"). It must read on its own. Keep it to about 24 characters with numbers.

data.name: TimingDetail
data.comment: The second line of the Timing panel's readout, under TimingHeadline: the speed the length comes from. {0} the speed ("30 fps", "2 s per photo"). It must read on its own after the headline.

data.name: PreviewPlay
data.comment: The screen reader name and tooltip of the preview's play button while the preview is paused (a verb: start playing the preview).

data.name: PreviewPause
data.comment: The same button while the preview plays (a verb).

data.name: PreviewScrubberName
data.comment: The screen reader name of the preview's slider, which picks which frame (one picture of the video) the preview shows. Not the Frame panel (the video's shape).

data.name: PositionOfTotal
data.comment: A place and the total, shown in small digits: the preview's frame counter ({0} "0312", {1} "0742") and the first-launch timelapse's time ({0} "00:10.40", {1} "00:24.73"). Keep the slash unless your language writes such counters otherwise.

data.name: FrameOfTotal
data.comment: A frame's place in the video (a frame is one picture of the video): the filmstrip's caption ({0} "0312", {1} "0742", zero-padded to keep their width) and the frame counter as a screen reader reads it ({0} "312", {1} "742").

data.name: PreviewTimecodeNameFormat
data.comment: The preview's time as a screen reader reads it. {0} the time in the video ("00:10.40"), {1} the video's length ("00:24.73").

data.name: PreviewPlaceholderFormat
data.comment: Drawn in the preview in place of a photo that cannot be read. {0} its file name ("IMG_4402.JPG"). No final period.

data.name: PreviewUnreadablePhotos_one
data.value: {0} photo can't be read, so the preview shows a placeholder for it. Restore or replace it before you export.
data.comment: A message bar while previewing; its list names the photos. {0} the number of photos ("1").

data.name: PreviewUnreadablePhotos_other
data.value: {0} photos can't be read, so the preview shows placeholders for them. Restore or replace them before you export.
data.comment: A message bar while previewing; its list names the photos. {0} the number of photos ("3").

data.name: PreviewCacheFailed
data.value: Preview copies of your photos can't be saved, so the preview may be slow. Your photos and the export aren't affected.
data.comment: A message bar: the small preview copies cannot be written to disk, so the preview reads the photos themselves, slower.

data.name: AddPhotos
data.comment: A command bar button (with an icon) that opens a menu: Choose folder, Choose photos, Include subfolders. Keep it to about 16 characters: the command bar is full at the smallest window (640 px).

data.name: ChooseFolder
data.comment: An item of the Add photos menu that opens the folder picker. The ellipsis says a picker opens.

data.name: ChoosePhotos
data.comment: An item of the Add photos menu that opens the file picker. The ellipsis says a picker opens.

data.name: IncludeSubfolders
data.comment: A toggle in the Add photos menu: also look for photos in the subfolders of a chosen or dropped folder.

data.name: ImportLooking
data.comment: The import progress in the command bar while the first photos are being looked for.

data.name: ImportFound_one
data.comment: The import progress in the command bar while photos are being listed. {0} the photos found so far ("1"). Keep it to about 30 characters with numbers: at the smallest window it wraps to a second line, then ends in an ellipsis.

data.name: ImportFound_other
data.comment: The same. {0} the photos found so far ("1,240"). Keep it to about 30 characters with numbers.

data.name: ImportAdding_one
data.comment: The import progress in the command bar while the photos are read, when there is one. {0} the photos read so far: English leaves {0} out because with one photo it says nothing the progress bar does not; leave it out too. {1} all of them ("1"; also "0" in languages whose _one form covers 0, as French and Brazilian Portuguese). Keep it to about 30 characters.

data.name: ImportAdding_other
data.comment: The import progress in the command bar while the photos are read; the form follows {1}. {0} the photos read so far ("1,240"), {1} all of them ("5,000"). Keep it to about 30 characters with numbers: at the smallest window (640 px) it wraps to a second line, then ends in an ellipsis.

data.name: ImportCancelName
data.comment: The screen reader name of the import progress's Cancel button.

data.name: ImportDone_one
data.comment: Read by a screen reader when an import ends. {0} the photos the project holds now ("1").

data.name: ImportDone_other
data.comment: Read by a screen reader when an import ends. {0} the photos the project holds now ("742").

data.name: DragCaptionAny
data.comment: The caption next to the pointer while files are dragged over the window, when their number is not known yet (folders). A command: drop to add photos.

data.name: DragCaptionPhotos_one
data.comment: The caption next to the pointer while photo files are dragged over the window. {0} the number of photos ("1"). Keep it short, about 20 characters.

data.name: DragCaptionPhotos_other
data.comment: The same. {0} the number of photos ("120"). Keep it short, about 20 characters.

data.name: DragCaptionSettingsOpen
data.comment: The caption next to the pointer while files are dragged over the window with the Settings page open: the drop is refused until the user leaves Settings.

data.name: DropTitle
data.value: Add these photos to this project?
data.comment: The title of the dialog a drop onto a project that has photos opens.

data.name: DropMessage_one
data.value: This project has {0} photo. Add the new photos to it, or start a new project with only the new ones. Starting a new project clears this one's photo and settings; the file stays on your PC.
data.comment: The drop dialog's message. {0} the number of photos the project has ("1").

data.name: DropMessage_other
data.value: This project has {0} photos. Add the new photos to it, or start a new project with only the new ones. Starting a new project clears this one's photos and settings; the files stay on your PC.
data.comment: The drop dialog's message. {0} the number of photos the project has ("742").

data.name: DropAddToProject
data.comment: The drop dialog's default button: add the dropped photos to the open project. Keep it to about 20 characters: the dialog's three buttons (with Start new project and Cancel) share its width.

data.name: ImportNothingFound
data.value: No photos 10Lapse can read were found there. Choose a folder or files with JPEG, PNG, TIFF or other photos, then try again.
data.comment: A message bar after an import found nothing to add.

data.name: ImportNothingFoundSubfoldersFormat
data.value: No photos were found in that folder. If they're in its subfolders, turn on {0} under {1}, then try again.
data.comment: A message bar after an import of a folder found nothing, with subfolders off. {0} the menu toggle's name (IncludeSubfolders, "Include subfolders"), {1} the menu's button (AddPhotos, "Add photos").

data.name: ImportAlreadyAdded
data.value: Those photos are already in this project.
data.comment: A message bar: every photo found was in the project already.

data.name: ImportStoppedNone
data.value: Stopped adding photos. None were added.
data.comment: A message bar after the user stopped an import before any photo was added.

data.name: ImportStoppedAdded_one
data.value: Stopped adding photos. {0} photo was added.
data.comment: A message bar after the user stopped an import. {0} the photos added before it stopped ("1").

data.name: ImportStoppedAdded_other
data.value: Stopped adding photos. {0} photos were added.
data.comment: A message bar after the user stopped an import. {0} the photos added before it stopped ("1,240").

data.name: ImportFolderFailedNamed
data.value: Couldn't open the folder {0}. Check that its drive or memory card is connected and that you can open it in File Explorer, then add it again.
data.comment: A message bar: one folder of the import would not open, or was no longer there. {0} the folder's name ("DCIM"), or a drive's path ("E:\").

data.name: ImportFoldersNotOpened_other
data.value: Couldn't open {0} folders. Check that their drives or memory cards are connected and that you can open them in File Explorer, then add them again.
data.comment: A message bar: several folders of the import would not open; its list names them. {0} the number of folders, always 2 or more ("3"), so English has no _one form.

data.name: CloudDownloadTitle
data.comment: The title of the dialog an import opens when some photos are only in OneDrive, not on the PC yet.

data.name: CloudDownloadQuestion_one
data.value: {0} photo is only in OneDrive. Download it now? About {1}.
data.comment: The OneDrive dialog's message. {0} the number of photos ("1"), {1} their size ("12 MB").

data.name: CloudDownloadQuestion_other
data.value: {0} photos are only in OneDrive. Download them now? About {1}.
data.comment: The OneDrive dialog's message. {0} the number of photos ("1,240"), {1} their size ("2.4 GB").

data.name: CloudDownloadConfirm
data.comment: The OneDrive dialog's button that downloads the photos and adds them (a verb). Keep it to about 16 characters.

data.name: CloudDownloadSkip_one
data.comment: The OneDrive dialog's default button: leave the photo in OneDrive and list it as skipped. {0} the number of photos: English leaves {0} out because the count is always 1 here; leave it out too. Keep it to about 16 characters.

data.name: CloudDownloadSkip_other
data.comment: The same for several photos. {0} the number of photos: English leaves {0} out of this button (the message above says it); leave it out too. Keep it to about 16 characters.

data.name: CodecGetFromStore
data.comment: The button of a message bar about a missing photo extension. It opens the extension's page in the Microsoft Store app; 10Lapse downloads nothing. "it" is the extension the message names; a wording without a pronoun is fine ("Open in the Store"). Keep it to about 24 characters.

data.name: CodecFree
data.comment: A free extension as the codec sentences name it, in the style of the Store listing ("HEIF Image Extensions (free)"). {0} its Store name, from StoreExtensionText. The name may be singular or plural; write the price as a label that does not agree with it, as the Store writes a price.

data.name: CodecFee
data.comment: An extension the Store sells, as the codec sentences name it, in the style of the Store listing ("HEVC Video Extensions (paid)"). {0} its Store name, from StoreExtensionText. The name may be singular or plural; write the price as a label that does not agree with it, as the Store writes a price.

data.name: CodecNeedsOne_one
data.comment: A message bar after an import: photos need one extension from the Microsoft Store. {0} the number of photos: English leaves {0} out because the count is always 1 here; leave it out too. {1} the extension as CodecFree or CodecFee ("HEIF Image Extensions (free)"). The name may be singular or plural; write the sentence so no article or pronoun has to agree with it.

data.name: CodecNeedsOne_other
data.comment: The same for several photos. {0} the number of photos ("12"), {1} the extension as CodecFree or CodecFee. The name may be singular or plural; write the sentence so no article or pronoun has to agree with it.

data.name: CodecNeedsSeveral_one
data.value: This photo needs {1} extensions from Microsoft. Start with {2}.
data.comment: A message bar after an import: photos need several extensions, installed one after the other with its button. {0} the number of photos: English leaves {0} out because the count is always 1 here; leave it out too. {1} the number of extensions (2 or more, "2"), {2} the first one as CodecFree or CodecFee. The name may be singular or plural; write the sentence so no article or pronoun has to agree with it.

data.name: CodecNeedsSeveral_other
data.value: These {0} photos need {1} extensions from Microsoft. Start with {2}.
data.comment: The same for several photos. {0} the number of photos ("8"), {1} the number of extensions (2 or more, "2"), {2} the first one as CodecFree or CodecFee. The name may be singular or plural; write the sentence so no article or pronoun has to agree with it.

data.name: CodecNextFormat
data.comment: The message bar after the user opened one extension's Store page, when more than one is still to come. {0} the next extension as CodecFree or CodecFee. The name may be singular or plural; write the sentence so no article or pronoun has to agree with it.

data.name: CodecLastFormat
data.value: Finally, get {0}. When the install finishes, restart 10Lapse and add the photos again.
data.comment: The message bar after the user opened one extension's Store page, when one is left. {0} the last extension as CodecFree or CodecFee. The name may be singular or plural; write the sentence so no article or pronoun has to agree with it.

data.name: CodecStoreFallbackFormat
data.value: Couldn't open the Microsoft Store. Search the Store for {0} and install the extension, then restart 10Lapse and add the photos again.
data.comment: A message bar when Windows could not open the Store page. {0} the extension's Store name to search for ("HEVC Video Extensions"), exactly as the Store writes it. The name may be singular or plural; write the sentence so no article or pronoun has to agree with it.

data.name: FirstLaunchTitle
data.value: Drop a folder of photos to make a timelapse
data.comment: The large title of the first-launch screen. No final period.

data.name: FirstLaunchDropTitle
data.comment: The same title while photos are dragged over the window. No final period.

data.name: FirstLaunchExplanationFormat
data.value: {0} plays your photos back as a video. Shoot one photo every few seconds, and {1} of them become a {3}-second clip at {2} frames per second.
data.comment: What a timelapse is, under the first-launch title. {0} the product name (10Lapse), {1} a number of photos ("300"), {2} a frame rate ("30"), {3} the clip's whole seconds ("10"). The numbers are fixed, so plural forms follow them in English (300, 10, 30).

data.name: FirstLaunchPrivacy
data.value: Your photos never leave this PC.
data.comment: The privacy line under the first-launch buttons.

data.name: FirstLaunchChooseFolder
data.comment: The first-launch screen's main button: opens the folder picker (as ChooseFolder, without the ellipsis). Keep it to about 18 characters.

data.name: FirstLaunchChoosePhotos
data.comment: The first-launch screen's second button: opens the file picker (as ChoosePhotos, without the ellipsis). Keep it to about 18 characters.

data.name: FilmstripName
data.comment: The screen reader name of the strip of thumbnails under the preview: the project's frames in order.

data.name: FilmstripItemNameFormat
data.comment: A thumbnail's name for a screen reader. {0} its frame number from 1, not padded ("312"), {1} the photo's file name ("IMG_0312.JPG").

data.name: FilmstripCaptionSelected_other
data.comment: The caption over the filmstrip with several frames selected. {0} how many frames are selected, always 2 or more ("3"), so English has no _one form; {1} the frame caption (FrameOfTotal, "Frame 0312 of 0742").

data.name: FilmstripFileTimeFormat
data.comment: The file caption over the filmstrip. {0} the file name, {1} the time the photo was taken, in your regional time format ("19:26:05").

data.name: FilmstripGapMissing_one
data.value: {0} photo seems to be missing before this one: the file numbers skip one.
data.comment: A gap marker's tooltip in the filmstrip (also read by a screen reader). {0} how many file numbers are skipped ("1").

data.name: FilmstripGapMissing_other
data.value: {0} photos seem to be missing before this one: the file numbers skip {0}.
data.comment: The same. {0} how many file numbers are skipped ("3").

data.name: FilmstripGapPause
data.value: Photos may be missing before this one: it was taken {0} after the one before, where about {1} was usual.
data.comment: A gap marker's tooltip for a long pause between two photos. {0} the pause ("2 min 10 s"), {1} the usual one ("5.0 s").

data.name: FilmstripPlayheadStatus
data.comment: Read by a screen reader for the thumbnail the preview shows.

data.name: FilmstripRemove
data.comment: A filmstrip context menu item: removes the selected frames from the project; the photos stay on disk. The Delete key does the same.

data.name: FilmstripUndo
data.comment: A filmstrip context menu item when there is nothing to undo (shown dimmed). Ctrl+Z does the same.

data.name: FilmstripMoveEarlier
data.comment: A filmstrip context menu item: moves the selected frames one place earlier in the video. Alt+Left does the same.

data.name: FilmstripMoveLater
data.comment: A filmstrip context menu item: moves the selected frames one place later. Alt+Right does the same.

data.name: FilmstripRemoveKeys
data.comment: The key shown beside Remove from project in the menu: the Delete key, as Windows names it on a keyboard of your language ("Entf" in German).

data.name: FilmstripUndoKeys
data.comment: The keys shown beside Undo in the menu and named in FilmstripRemovedFrames. The letter is fixed; translate only "Ctrl", as Windows names that key on a keyboard of your language ("Strg" in German).

data.name: FilmstripMoveEarlierKeys
data.comment: The keys shown beside Move earlier: Alt and the Left arrow key, as Windows names them in your language.

data.name: FilmstripMoveLaterKeys
data.comment: The keys shown beside Move later: Alt and the Right arrow key, as Windows names them in your language.

data.name: FilmstripThumbnailSize
data.comment: The screen reader name of the slider that sets the filmstrip's thumbnail size.

data.name: FilmstripRemovedFrames_one
data.value: Removed {0} frame from the project. The photo stays on your PC. {1} puts it back.
data.comment: Read by a screen reader after a removal. {0} how many frames were removed ("1"), {1} the undo keys (FilmstripUndoKeys, "Ctrl+Z").

data.name: FilmstripRemovedFrames_other
data.value: Removed {0} frames from the project. The photos stay on your PC. {1} puts them back.
data.comment: The same. {0} how many frames were removed ("3"), {1} the undo keys ("Ctrl+Z").

data.name: FilmstripRestoredFrames_one
data.comment: Read by a screen reader after an undo put removed frames back. {0} how many ("1").

data.name: FilmstripRestoredFrames_other
data.comment: The same. {0} how many ("3").

data.name: FilmstripRestoredNone
data.value: Nothing to put back: those photos are in the project again.
data.comment: Read by a screen reader after an undo of a removal found every photo back in the project already (imported again).

data.name: FilmstripUndoRemove_one
data.comment: The filmstrip context menu's Undo after a removal. {0} the number of frames removed ("1"). No final period.

data.name: FilmstripUndoRemove_other
data.comment: The same. {0} the number of frames removed ("12"). No final period.

data.name: FilmstripUndoMove
data.comment: The filmstrip context menu's Undo after frames were moved. No final period.

data.name: FilmstripReorderUndone
data.value: Put the frames back in their earlier order.
data.comment: Read by a screen reader after an undo of a move.

data.name: FilmstripNothingToUndo
data.comment: Read by a screen reader when Ctrl+Z has nothing to undo.

data.name: FilmstripMovedFrame
data.comment: Read by a screen reader after one frame was moved. {0} its frame number before the move ("12"), {1} its place now, from 1 ("11").

data.name: FilmstripMovedFrames_other
data.comment: Read by a screen reader after several frames were moved. {0} how many, always 2 or more ("3"), so English has no _one form; {1} the first one's place now, from 1.
